reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because the speaker's main action is warning beginners about cloud-mining schemes and investigating whether advertised mining returns are plausible. He identifies sites as suspected Ponzi schemes, tests their claimed payments, explains how to research companies, and states that unusually high mining returns are fake. Although he discusses and tentatively recommends some services, the overall message is critical and cautionary rather than an invitation to participate.

opening.argument: The video repeatedly connects paid mining participation with recurring cryptocurrency returns. One displayed plan promises 200% profit over four months and says the viewer must activate the machine daily, making the income conditional on continued participation. Another page presents lifetime Bitcoin packages with prices, hash rates, and account-creation buttons. A separate mining site pairs “Daily earning” with a “START MINING” button and a sign-up sequence. Taken together, this is not merely discussion of mining technology: it shows viewers a concrete path to buy mining capacity, activate it, and receive recurring returns.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a warning does not change what the demonstrations place in front of viewers: priced mining packages, sign-up controls, activation instructions, and stated returns. The speaker also says he recommends named mining services, so the presentation supplies actionable alternatives rather than only discouraging participation. The central viewer takeaway can therefore be an invitation to choose a mining plan, not simply an investigation.

citations.quote: I recommend Gens Smiley and Rich Flay.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The displayed offers are evidence being examined, not promises made by the speaker. The speaker explicitly warns beginners, identifies many sites as Ponzi schemes, and rejects unusually high returns as fake. His recommendation is limited to services he presents as having observable mining evidence, while the surrounding discussion repeatedly tells viewers to investigate before investing.

citations.quote: This video is to warn to beginners that are entering into the world of cryptocurrencies
Most of these sites are ponzu schemes
Nothing greater than that is a fake.

opening.argument: The combination of unusually large returns, crypto mining packages, and direct participation controls is a strong deception signal. A plan shown on screen advertises 200% profit in four months while requiring daily machine activation. Another page labels paid packages “Lifetime Bitcoin plan,” assigns them substantial hash rates and dollar prices, and offers account creation. A separate site promises daily earnings and tells the viewer to sign up, choose cloud, and start mining. Even if individual claims are presented as examples, this combination normalizes purchasing mining capacity on the strength of attractive recurring returns.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference account emphasizes criticism but underweights the promotional force of showing the offers in usable detail. Viewers see the prices, capacities, returns, sign-up buttons, and operational steps needed to participate. The speaker's statement that he recommends two services further weakens the claim that the material functions only as a warning.

citations.quote: I recommend Gens Smiley and Rich Flay.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The risk signals are presented precisely to expose implausible offers. The speaker says a 5% daily mining profit is impossible, describes non-paying sites, and explains that high returns exceed what mining can generate. Showing a page's claims alongside calculations and criticism is investigative context, not endorsement of those claims.

opening.argument: The apparent review format also functions as promotion because it guides viewers toward selected mining services. The speaker says he will provide website links, recommends specific companies, and contrasts them with other services. The footage reinforces that funnel: a mining site says to register and start earning, while another displays paid lifetime packages with “CREATE ACCOUNT” controls. The video therefore does more than report on scams; it curates supposedly acceptable providers and demonstrates how viewers can enter the mining market.

citations.quote: I will also write some links of some websites in the video description
I recommend Gens Smiley and Rich Flay.

rebuttal.rebuttal: A warning label is not dispositive when the same presentation supplies links, names preferred providers, and displays the mechanics of registration and account creation. The speaker's favorable distinction between selected services and the rest can steer viewers toward those services. That selective steering is consistent with promotion even when surrounded by negative commentary about competitors.

citations.quote: I will also write some links of some websites in the video description
I recommend Gens Smiley and Rich Flay.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The links and recommendations are framed as resources for further information, while the speaker repeatedly says he does not recommend the cloud-mining sites generally and urges company research. He distinguishes services based on evidence such as visible mining machines, not on a guaranteed profit pitch. The overall role remains cautionary because the alleged offers are tested and criticized rather than presented as safe purchases.
